title: In 1934, One Mountain Recorded a 231 Mile an Hour Wind

scenes.text: A mountain once recorded a 231 mile an hour wind.
It was Mount Washington in New Hampshire, on April 12, 1934.
That is stronger than any category five hurricane.
The crew still climbed outside to chip ice off the wind gauge.
Then they timed three clicks on a stopwatch to work out the speed.
That number stood as the world record for over sixty years.

description:
On April 12, 1934, the weather observatory on Mount Washington measured a 231 mile an hour gust.
The staff worked out the speed with a stopwatch, and it stood as the world record for over sixty years.
Would you stand outside in that? Comment below.
first_comment: 231 miles an hour, measured by hand. How strong a wind have you ever stood in?
